solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Organs and head of toad stored in glass bottles

indicators.note: the toad's first letter is kept inside the bottles, so it goes into the other word

parts.note: vials are small glass bottles

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from toad

explanation.surface: A grisly lab where a toad's organs and head are pickled in jars.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital organs such as heart and lungs are informally called the vitals.

clue.text: Plain article in nice house

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the house, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a villa is a fine, desirable house
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone describes a tasteful but unremarkable piece of furniture in a pleasant home.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is slang for ordinary or unadorned, as in a plain vanilla version.

clue.text: Woman's property act finally getting support of Swiss philosopher

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word act

parts.note: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was a Geneva-born philosopher

explanation.surface: A legal act about a woman's possessions wins backing from a famous Swiss thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting support of' is a link: in a down clue the philosopher sits under the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride brings to her marriage, her own goods.

clue.text: Ladies say little Edward stole stuff

parts.note: the Ladies is an example of a toilet, a loo in British slang
Ted is a short, familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: Women gossip that a boy called Edward has been pilfering.
explanation.definitionFit: To have looted is to have plundered, carrying off goods unlawfully.

clue.text: Daily traveller being firm with silent, boring man

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: boring means drilling through, so the silent word goes into the middle of the man

parts.note: Mr, mister, is the title of a man
mute means making no sound

explanation.surface: A daily traveller sits in a company car with a quiet, dull man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull but means piercing: MUTE goes into MR.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter travels to and from work each day, a regular daily journey.

clue.text: Nil, really oddly, by mouth

parts.note: nil is zero, shown as the letter O

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions of the word really

explanation.surface: Someone stresses that nothing at all is to be taken by mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral describes something given or taken through the mouth, like medicine.

clue.text: Neighbours get hold of out-of-date eggs from eastern Europe

indicators.note: to get hold of is to grasp, so the neighbouring pair wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: M and N are neighbours in the alphabet
old means out of date, no longer current
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: People next door are handed stale eggs that came from eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbours' looks like people next door; it is the adjacent letters M and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Moldova is a country in eastern Europe, so something Moldovan comes from there.

clue.text: Teach trout to swim

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so the word trout is rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to coach a fish in swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to teach a pupil privately, giving one-to-one instruction.

clue.text: Their science is notoriously hard and moves fast

definitions.meaning: rocket science is the proverbial example of something very difficult
to rocket is to shoot upward or forward at great speed

explanation.definitionFit: Rocket science is the byword for difficulty, and rockets as a verb means speeds along.

clue.text: Right-winger has one nasty trick

indicators.note: nasty suggests something turned bad, a sign to rearrange the word one

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick

explanation.surface: A conservative politician is said to hold a dirty trick up the sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A neocon, a neoconservative, belongs to a hawkish faction of the political right.

clue.text: Artfully flexible reinterpretation of libel act

indicators.note: a reinterpretation recasts something, so the letters of libel act are reordered

explanation.surface: A court takes a fresh, nimble reading of defamation law.
explanation.definitionFit: Balletic describes graceful agility like that of a ballet dancer.

clue.text: Seduce bloke in train carriage

parts.note: to pull is British slang for attracting a romantic partner
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A romantic encounter on a railway journey.
explanation.walkthrough: PULL in this sense is British informal for picking someone up; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pullman is a luxurious railway carriage, named after George Pullman.

clue.text: Side has good lead, so pay attention!

parts.note: L stands for left, one side
is stands in for has in a phrase like he is ahead
being ten up, ten points ahead, is a good lead

explanation.surface: A team is comfortably ahead, so the coach demands their attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Listen up is an informal command telling people to pay attention.

clue.text: Neighbour's expertly hedging stock market

indicators.note: hedging means enclosing, as a hedge encloses a field, so the run sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A neighbour skilfully hedges bets on the stock exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedging' looks like a financial term; it is enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bourse is a stock exchange, especially one in continental Europe such as Paris.

clue.text: British-Brazilian couple upside down in bedroom

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: Rio, short for Rio de Janeiro, stands for a Brazilian here
a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Brazilian pair end up tumbling about in a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A boudoir is a lady's private bedroom or dressing room.

clue.text: Categorise missing leader as "Third Man"

indicators.note: missing its leader means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to label is to categorise or classify

explanation.surface: Someone is filed under the title of the famous film, minus its star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third Man' suggests the film; in Genesis Abel is the third man, after Adam and Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: After Adam and his firstborn Cain, the next male in the Bible is Abel, making him the third.

clue.text: Everything was once distributed in rations

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of was once are scattered

explanation.surface: Wartime nostalgia: everything used to be handed out under rationing.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowances are fixed amounts given out, just as rations are allotted shares.

clue.text: Cutting delivery?

parts.note: looks like a sharp remark or a severed shipment; really a birth by surgical incision

explanation.definitionFit: A Caesarean section delivers a baby by cutting through the abdomen.

clue.text: I pay periodically to enter London landmark, birthplace of Queen Elizabeth?

indicators.note: to enter means to go into, so these letters are placed inside the landmark

parts.note: the Shard is a glass skyscraper by London Bridge

indicators.note: periodically picks every other letter of the word pay

explanation.surface: A tourist pays now and then to get into a London sight linked to royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Elizabeth' suggests the monarch; it is the liner, built at a shipyard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen Elizabeth liners were built in a shipyard, where ships are born.

clue.text: US star who'd fallen down

indicators.note: a fallen thing has collapsed into disorder, so the letters of US star who'd are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American celebrity who would have tumbled from fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading southwards means going down the map, so down is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Carpets displayed bands of colours

indicators.note: displayed means spread out for show, so the letters of carpets are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Rugs are shown off, revealing stripes of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectra are the bands of colour seen when light is split, as in a rainbow.

clue.text: Unaffected, like the Queen on vacation

indicators.note: vacation is emptying out, here clearing the middle letter from the word

parts.note: regal means like a queen or king, royal

explanation.surface: A remark that the monarch on holiday is quite down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' hints at a holiday; here it means emptying the middle out, removing the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A real person is genuine and natural, free of pretence or affectation.

clue.text: Uppsala MBA student, full of rubbish

indicators.note: the words are full of the answer, which runs through them

explanation.surface: A business student at a Swedish university is talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to criticise harshly. Uppsala is a Swedish university town.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast is to attack severely in words, the way critics rubbish a show.

clue.text: Piece of music wears thin for listener

indicators.note: for a listener means as heard, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: fabric that frays wears thin at the edges

explanation.surface: A tune grows tiresome to the person hearing it.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a phrase is a short passage forming a unit of melody.

clue.text: Supplies Ecstasy pills cut with crack

indicators.note: drugs cut with another substance have it mixed in, so the joke goes inside the pills

parts.note: E is ecstasy; more than one pill makes Es
a crack is a witty remark, a quip

explanation.surface: A dealer supplies ecstasy tablets adulterated with crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the drug, fitting the surface; it is a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to supply with what is needed, as equips with tools.

clue.text: Cheerful group becoming unhappy

parts.note: up means in good spirits
a set is a group or collection

explanation.surface: A jolly gathering turns sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset means being distressed and unhappy.

clue.text: Place to bring eggs to fry?

definitions.text: Place to bring eggs to fry?

parts.words: Place to bring eggs to fry?
parts.note: suggests a kitchen; fry are young fish, raised from spawn at a fishery

explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm hatches roe and rears the young fish, called fry, for food.

clue.text: Stanley perhaps left drink

definitions.meaning: ... Stanley, the Falkland Islands capital, is an example of a harbour town
the left side of a ship facing forward

explanation.definitionFit: Port names a harbour town such as Stanley, a ship's left side, and a fortified wine.

clue.text: Will man check roster on return?

parts.note: to test is to check

indicators.note: on return means coming back, so the word for roster is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man called Will can check the duty roster when he gets back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a first name; it is a legal will, and its man is the one who makes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who has made a will, the will's author.

clue.text: Drive into Florida shanty town

indicators.note: into means the street word goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Ave, avenue, is a kind of street like a drive

explanation.surface: A motorist heads into Florida and finds a slum.
explanation.definitionFit: A favela is a Brazilian slum, a shanty town of makeshift housing.

clue.text: Counter-agent has Sunday off, stationed abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are rearranged
off means taken away, so the Sunday letter is removed

explanation.surface: A secret agent posted overseas gets a Sunday off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes S from STATIONED, leaving TATIONED, which 'abroad' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counteracts a poison, so it is literally a counter-agent.

clue.text: Exercise freak eating a snack

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the a goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a nut is a fanatic or freak, as in fitness nut

explanation.surface: A gym fanatic tucks into something.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is a common salted snack eaten from a packet.
